what: The Buy tab (spec/pages.md §6.12): one search box, then the shelves Needs you, New matches, Looking for, Watching and Bought. Nothing here commits the person without a tap.
frame: Who: the hunter (personas: Hunting one thing), opening it when an alert lands or a few times a week; the person clearing out, with one want running.
Came to do: see what turned up for what they want and act before it is gone, or start a new search.
Where a mistake costs most: an offer that binds them on eBay once accepted, and a good match missed because it was buried.
Ways out (spec/ways-out.md §6.12): every listing opens on its site; offers ask every time; a want pauses from its page; Not my size from the listing.
In the loop: the agent's offer waits on the card with its amount on the button, and after the tap it holds for 5 s with Undo before it goes.
decisions: No wash: the wash holds no control (constitution Art. 5, The wash), and the search box is this page's first control.
Needs you shows only the buy-side asks (the waiting offer and a match over the most); did-you-buy and sign-in warnings stay on Today, where every card already is.
The waiting offer is the lead card: it is the one thing on the page that waits on the person, and its button says the amount it sends.
Send holds the offer 5 s in the toast with Undo before it goes (Gmail's Undo Send), because a sent offer cannot be pulled back on the site.
A found listing is a MatchCard, not an ItemCard: it has no state of the person's to tag, and its read of the price is words with an icon because no state color means fair (round-2 call).

Each want is an item card whose tag says how its search stands: '3 of 4 sites' while one is still answering, 'Searching' when all are in, 'Paused'; its fact says what it found under the most, or 'Nothing yet'.
A want with no product photo takes the photo of the newest thing it found, else the empty photo slot: never a made-up picture.
Over your most: the primary act is Walk away, the agent's suggestion; raising the most is the second and is the person's own limit, so it saves with Undo.
Worlds: ?world=buyer is the hunter; no world is clearing (one want, nothing found); ?world=new is empty. Every link keeps the world.
Loading is the page's skeleton, failed says what did not load with Try again, and offline keeps the last copy under 'Waiting for signal' (app/src/buy/states.tsx), the same on every buy page.

A want's card is titled with what it is ("Standing desk"), not the sentence it was typed as: the most is already on its line ("Nothing yet under $150") and the distance and size are on the want's page. Art. 7.15, check U14; a bought thing takes its short name the same way.
